newsitem.title: USA: Tower Air France and San Juan services.
newsitem.headline: Tower Air France and San Juan services.

text.p: Tower Air handles an average of 20 tonnes of Dutch perishable commodities on each of its flights from Paris to New York, David Cooper, General Manager for Mercury Air Cargo Group, Eastern U.S. told Reuters.

Mercury Air Cargo, Tower's cargo general sales agent, said the Dutch perishables, that do not include flowers, are trucked daily to Paris before being loaded onto the carrier's Boeing 747-200s and 100s it uses for the daily flights.

An average of 7 tonnes of freight per flight leaves New York daily for Paris, Cooper said. He attributes the light cargo load ex-New York to the fact that the group only began selling that space exclusively since May of this year.

The carrier, from the eastern seaboard, is also serving Paris twice-weekly from Baltimore, Boston and Miami. Cooper said each of those flights are at full cargo load returning to the U.S. with Dutch perishables.

On its daily New York - San Juan trips, Cooper said the B747-200s are at approximately 75 percent load factor in both directions. They usually carry "general consolidated cargo freight," he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
